docs.title: Description
docs.text:
mint is a boilerplate scaffold tool designed for

  • Flask
  • Servlets

Get started with: 

mint --help
Usage: mint [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options:
  --help  Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  flask
  servlet

The sub-commands available are flask and servlet, each sub-command expects a required argument FOLDER FOLDER here is the target directory where boilerplate is generated. The directory should be non-existent or should be empty for mint to scaffold in it.

So the structure is: 

mint [OPTIONS] COMMAND <FOLDER> [ARGS]

docs.title: Flask
docs.text:
The directory structure for flask boilerplate is as:

flask-project
├── app.py
├── static
└── templates
    ├── base.html
    └── index.html

3 directories, 3 files

This is the default structure expected by flask and each of the files generated here are populated with template content.

Boilerplate within app.py is as: 

from flask import Flask, render_template

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route('/')
def index():
    return render_template('index.html')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(debug=True)

Similarly other files are also populated in flask boilerplate to scaffold a ready to run template project.

docs.title: Servlets
docs.text:
Servlet boilerplate generation is more aligned with legacy way of handling servlets. 

Usage: mint servlet [OPTIONS] FOLDER

Options:
  -n, --number INTEGER  Specify number of servlet objects in web.xml
  --no-xml              Opt out of generating web.xml
  --index               Generate index.html
  --help                Show this message and exit.

Default template structure: 

template-servlet
└── WEB-INF
    ├── classes
    └── web.xml

The file web.xml here is populated with one servlet inside the root web-app element as: 

<web-app>
<servlet>
  <servlet-name></servlet-name>
  <servlet-class></servlet-class>
</servlet>
<servlet-mapping>
  <servlet-name></servlet-name>
  <url-pattern></url-pattern>
</servlet-mapping>
</web-app>

docs.title: --number option
docs.text:
The number of servlet elements in the file can be controlled with the -n (shorthand for --number) as: 

mint servlet -n 3 template-servlet

This produces 3 servlet elements within the root element web-app

docs.title: --no-xml flag
docs.text:
You can use the --no-xml flag to opt out of generating web.xml in the boilerplate as: 

mint servlet --no-xml template-servlet

so the structure would be:

template-servlet
└── WEB-INF
    └── classes

docs.title: --index flag
docs.text:
The --index flag is used to generate an index.html at the boilerplate root 

mint servlet --index servlet-1

so the structure would be 

servlet-1
├── WEB-INF
│   ├── classes
│   └── web.xml
└── index.html

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
Use our installer script 

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saikiranp-24/mint/main/install.sh | sh

or install with homebrew 

brew install saikiranp-24/tap/mint
or 
brew tap saikiranp-24/tap
brew install mint

docs.title: macOS
docs.text:
Install with homebrew 

brew install saikiranp-24/tap/mint
or 
brew tap saikiranp-24/tap
brew install mint

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
Install with scoop 

scoop bucket add saikiranp-24 https://github.com/saikiranp-24/scoop-bucket
scoop install saikiranp-24/mint

Alternatively, you could use uv on any of its supported platforms to install 

uv tool install git+https://github.com/saikiranp-24/mint
